messages.subject: Minor bug with initializations/bounded variables
parts:
This is a strange one which may not have an obvious solution, if any.
I've attached a simple model to demonstrate the problem.

If you do:

inittest --init=inittest.init --point_estimate

you'll see that the initial value of x is actually 1e35, instead of 1.
(The same thing, plus some noise, happens without the
point_estimate.) The problem is that the range of the bound is too
large and double precision is not enough to handle values that close
to one end. In a sense, there's nothing we can do here short of using
long doubles (which seems like definite overkill...)

There are two issues that I see here.

1) It would be nice to catch this kind of error with the
initialization and report it to the user.

2) If people unwittingly set really large bounds like this, the
sampling is likely to produce incorrect results if the posterior
probability is mostly located near one end of the bound or another due
to discretization. This should definitely be mentioned in the manual
and it might even be worth trying to figure out what the "largest"
range is and print a warning if it comes up at run time.

Cheers,
Marcus
